name: Montearagón castle (Huesca siege lines)
story: The 11th-century castle-abbey of Montearagón stands on a hill east of Huesca. From 1936 to 1938 it was part of the Republican ring around Nationalist-held Huesca, together with the Estrecho Quinto bunker below. Its commanding views over the city made it an important observation and defensive position for the Republican columns and, later, the Popular Army. The front moved away only when the Nationalist offensive of March 1938 broke the siege lines.
see: Massive medieval walls on a hilltop with views over Huesca and the siege ground. Civil War remains are nearby.
plan: Guided visits only (about €5), in several sessions a day. Book by phone (622 573 497) or online.
